quotes.text: A fee that Connect platforms collect from connected accounts for each payment or payout.

An event delivered with a complete Event object and a point-in-time snapshot of the related resource. Its payload follows the API version configured for the event destination, and the snapshot might be outdated when you process it.
Stripe supports OUSD and USDC for stablecoin balances, although transfers on the Tempo network use USDC.e.
A Stripe balance held in OUSD or USDC stablecoin.
Thin event notifications aren't tied to an API version.

old_evidence.text: A fee that Connect platforms collect from connected accounts for each payment they receive.
A cryptocurrency that's pegged to the value of a fiat currency or other asset in order to limit volatility.
A webhook is a real-time push notification sent to your application as a JSON payload through HTTPS requests.

findings: The new capture has 286 one-line glossary entries (new lines 9–294) versus 240 two-line entries in the old capture (old lines 5–725). The diff is largely a wholesale formatting replacement, but there are genuine added terms and definition changes. Literal label-set differences include case, escaping, and renamed labels, so neither a textual omission nor a raw 60-new/15-old label count is evidence of product deprecation.

The application fee definition expands from each payment the platform receives (old 53–54) to each payment or payout (new 24). Current source line 66 says per payment only; update that row with the payout scope and the dated new raw reference, without asserting that every Connect integration charges both kinds of fee.

The new capture adds snapshot event (244) and thin event (273): a snapshot includes a point-in-time related-resource payload governed by the event destination API version and can be stale at processing time; a thin notification provides identifiers, requires retrieval for more data, and is not API-version-bound. The old webhook definition at 719–720 remains a general transport description and does not establish these event-specific semantics.

The stablecoin definition now names OUSD and USDC for Stripe balances and USDC.e for Tempo transfers (new 248), with separate asset, balance, custody, and issuance entries (249–252). The old definition (623–624) gave only the generic pegged-asset meaning. Treat these as dated glossary assertions, not independently verified current product availability, account eligibility, or a claim that assets on different networks are interchangeable.

The new glossary adds pricing-model, authorization/capture, release-phase, crypto, and routing vocabulary, including service interval (234), dimensional pricing (87), partial capture (41), frontier (116), and Orchestration (171, 260). The current source's 130+ description is true but outdated in precision; retain its compact thematic selection and add dated coverage only where useful. The glossary does not revise the detailed preview status or processor constraints retained in the separate Stripe Orchestration concept.
substantive_changes: Update [[source-stripe-glossary]] with the November 2026 raw reference and revise its application fee row to include payment or payout; give a dated, scoped summary of the newly defined event, stablecoin, pricing, and routing terms. The 286-versus-240 entry expansion is substantive despite the diff's full-list reformatting.

Keep glossary definitions separate from detailed operational guides. In particular, snapshot staleness versus thin-event retrieval is terminology, stablecoin network examples are capture-dated, and the new Orchestration entry says nothing about release availability or supported processors.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain raw/stripe-glossary-2025.md as the dated 240-entry capture and its older per-payment application fee wording; the newer wording expands scope rather than proving how any past integration was billed.
Preserve the old generic stablecoin definition as historical context and avoid reading new OUSD/USDC/USDC.e examples back into the 2025 capture.

Preserve the old general webhook definition and the source's established PaymentIntent, billing, and Connect terminology where the new glossary does not actually contradict it. A renamed or differently capitalized term is not evidence that its prior meaning was removed.

The glossary's full-list replacement and minor label normalization do not establish deprecation of old labels; any such claim would require product-specific evidence outside this review-only job.
